55673.label: Robin, the sidekick
55673.note: Every top sentence mentions Robin across his incarnations: Jason Todd in Dark Knight Returns and A Death in the Family, Dick Grayson christened Robin in Lego Batman, Tim Drake in Hush and Knightfall, the Robins in Batman Ninja, and the 'Batman and Robin' pairing in R.I.P. and Batman & Robin.

426468.label: Ra's al Ghul
426468.note: All eight sentences concern Ra's al Ghul and his family: Ducard revealed as Ra's, Crane working for him and his death on the train in Batman Begins, Talia revealed as his daughter and his wife's imprisonment in Dark Knight Rises, and the Lazarus Pits and his healing blood in Hush and Arkham City.

464175.label: Jason Todd (the name Jason)
464175.note: A layer-1 detector for the name 'Jason': six of eight sentences are Jason Todd, the second Robin killed by the Joker (Dark Knight Returns twice, Under the Red Hood, A Death in the Family twice, White Knight), with spillover onto botanist Jason Woodrue in Batman & Robin and the orphan Jason in Gotham by Gaslight.

496024.label: Jason Todd
496024.note: Fires on 'Todd': seven of eight sentences name Jason Todd, the second Robin, most of them about his death or its aftermath (murdered in Dark Knight Returns, tortured in White Knight, the trauma and fear-gas flashback in Knightfall, back from the dead in Hush), plus one 'Catherine Todd' line, so it is a surname detector.

477538.label: Mentions of 'Batman' (loose)
477538.note: No clear theme: six of eight sentences contain the word Batman, three of them with the name in quotes as what the press calls the vigilante (Batman '89, Earth One, Batman Begins), plus the Arkham City cast list, the Killing Joke comedian and A Death in the Family; the top sentence (Dent at the Monarch Theatre) and the Arkham Island setting line do not mention him at all.

60391.label: Words beginning with 'Qu'
60391.note: A spelling-level feature rather than story content: every top sentence contains a 'Qu' word (Lecter's 'quid pro quo', 'quell', alcalde Quintero in Zorro, Quetch, Harley Quinzel twice, Quincey Morris in Dracula, the 'Quake Engine'), and it fires on non-Batman films and cousins as readily as on Batman.

765185.label: Two-Face's coin
765185.note: Seven of eight sentences involve Two-Face's scarred coin deciding fates (four from the Arkham Asylum comic, including the therapy that swaps the coin for a die and tarot deck, plus Batman Forever and The Dark Knight); the eighth is Dent's acid disfigurement in Batman Forever, and it appears in no cousin.

13339.label: Selina Kyle
13339.note: All 8 top sentences name Selina, either in full or as just 'Selina' (the cat burglar stealing Bruce's fingerprints in Dark Knight Rises, the actress in Gotham by Gaslight, freeing Bruce as Catwoman in The Long Halloween, at the opera in Hush), and it never fires on a cousin; it is a name detector, present in 7 Batman works.

505173.label: Dick Grayson, the first Robin
505173.note: 7 of 8 top sentences name Dick Grayson (orphan of the Flying Graysons in Batman Forever, Nightwing in Under the Red Hood, 'the first Robin' in A Death in the Family, the adopted orphan in Lego Batman), and the eighth is an Arkham City cast list that only mentions Robin.

498697.label: The villain's lair
498697.note: Every top sentence contains the word 'lair' (Freeze's, the Riddler's twice, Killer Croc's sewer, Ra's al Ghul's underground lair, the 1943 gang's Fun House), and it also fires on Lex Luthor's lair in Superman, so this is the general villain's-hideout pattern rather than anything specific to Batman.

57687.label: Gotham's prisons and prisoners
57687.note: About 6 of 8 top sentences involve prisons or captives (Bane freeing Blackgate's prisoners, Bruce sentenced to Blackgate, Arkham City as a prison enclosure, Quinn freeing Ivy from her cell, the captured Bane, Chase held prisoner), but only 2 are actually about inmates being released, so the old label 'Prison and the inmates released' overclaims; the other two sentences are unrelated (Rocky's pet store, Alfred at Wayne Manor).

470135.label: Staging a scheme or fake
470135.note: 6 of 8 top sentences use 'stage' to mean setting something up (a staged prison fight, a suicide, Bruce's death, a kidnapping, Batman's plan with Gordon, Stane's coup in Iron Man), and only about 4 of those are actual fakes; the other 2 fire on the name 'Simon Stagg', so it partly reacts to the spelling, and plots like these are common to crime stories in general.

2047.label: The district attorney
2047.note: A first-layer neuron that reacts to the word 'district': 6 of 8 top sentences mention a (assistant) district attorney, 5 of them Harvey Dent and one Rachel, and the other two are 'red-light district' and 'a poverty-ridden district of Gotham', so it is really Harvey Dent's job title rather than a general idea.

93463.label: Arkham Asylum
93463.note: All 8 top sentences mention Arkham (the asylum on Arkham Island, Arkham Castle in Batman Ninja, the Arkham Knight's 'A' logo, Nygma and Freeze being committed there, patients taking over the facility), though one is an Arkham City cast list naming the earlier game, and it appears in 18 Batman works but only 1 cousin.

457852.label: Protocol 10 (Arkham City)
457852.note: 5 of 8 top sentences are about Hugo Strange's Protocol 10 scheme in Arkham City; the rest are near-misses on similar-sounding words ('protégé' Jason Todd twice, 'company policy' in Alien), so it is a narrow detector for one plot device in one game, and the near-misses are why it shows up in 6 Batman works.

520801.label: The butler who raised him
520801.note: All 8 top sentences name Alfred Pennyworth in full (the family butler in Joker 2019, raising Bruce in Batman Begins, head of security in Earth One, hurt by a letter bomb in The Batman), so it is really a name detector for Alfred and not the idea of a butler; it appears in 18 Batman works and just 1 cousin.

448712.label: The Joker's chemical origin
448712.note: A first-layer neuron for the word 'chemical': 6 of 8 top sentences are about the chemical plant behind the Joker's origin (Napier falling into a vat and the Axis Chemicals raids in Batman '89, the Killing Joke comedian's chemical company, his bleached skin), plus Ace Chemicals in Arkham Knight and the Green Goblin's chemical in Spider-Man; only one sentence describes the actual fall, so the old label 'Fell into a vat of chemicals' was narrowed to the origin as a whole.

16460.label: Bane
16460.note: All eight top sentences name Bane: his prison-raised supersoldier origin (Knightfall), his Dark Knight Rises schemes (Daggett, the stock exchange, his henchmen capturing Gordon), Woodrue turning Antonio Diego into Bane (Batman & Robin), and his fights in Arkham Asylum and Batman Ninja; only 1 of 13 cousins has it.

465435.label: The antidote
465435.note: Seven of eight sentences are about making or giving an antidote to a toxin (Fox's antidote in Batman Begins, Terry saving Bruce in Return of the Joker, Ivy's spores and the single dose in Arkham Asylum, Freeze's antidote in Arkham City); the odd one out is the Penguin's toxic heavy water in Batman '66; no cousins have it.

465641.label: Radium and the 'Bat-radia'
465641.note: Looks like a detector for the word shape 'radi-', not an idea: three sentences are about the stolen radium in the 1943 serial and three about the 'Bat-radia' in Batman R.I.P., but the other two (Percy's dandyish lifestyle in Scarlet Pimpernel, Bane injecting the Riddler with Venom) have nothing to do with either.

494307.label: Describing the video game
494307.note: Six of eight sentences are Wikipedia describing a game as a game ('The game features a large ensemble', 'The game also makes references', 'The game introduces the Arkham Knight', 'The game takes place in the center of the city', the Arkham Knight cameo list, the Mad Hatter being cut by the developers); the two Batman Ninja 'Quake Engine' sentences are plot and probably hit on the word 'Engine'; it follows the video-game medium, not Batman story content.

47532.label: A mutating super-formula
47532.note: All eight sentences contain 'mutate', 'mutated' or 'Mutants', but only about five involve a mutating chemical (the Titan formula in the Joker's blood and his Titan overdose in the Arkham games, Woodrue mutating Diego into Bane, toxins turning Isley into Poison Ivy); Killer Croc's worsening condition, the Dark Knight Returns 'Mutants' gang and the 'mutated gangster Killer Croc' cast list only share the word, so it may partly be a word detector; no cousins have it.

878889.label: Taking in an orphan as a ward
878889.note: Three sentences are explicitly about Bruce taking in orphans as wards or adopting them (the Gotham by Gaslight orphans, Dick moving into Wayne Manor in Batman Forever, Lego Batman adopting Dick), and three more are about the same arc (the Flying Graysons killed, Dick demanding to join Batman, Bruce accepting him as Robin); the Chase Meridian sentence and Barbara joining in Batman & Robin don't fit, and five of the eight come from Batman Forever; no cousins have it.

53042.label: The name 'Ace'
53042.note: A name detector that lumps two different Batman things together: Ace the Great Dane in Return of the Joker (three sentences) and the Ace Chemicals plant in Arkham Knight and Under the Red Hood (three sentences); two sentences (Jordan Pryce, the Arkham Asylum comic villain list) don't use the name; the 3 cousin hits are probably the ordinary word 'ace'.

43490.label: The Mad Hatter
43490.note: Six of eight sentences name the Mad Hatter (Napier using his mind-control technology in White Knight, his being cut from Arkham Asylum, the villain lists in The Long Halloween, the Arkham Asylum comic, Arkham City and Arkham Knight); the Star Wars and Pride & Prejudice sentences are stray noise; no cousins have it.

119563.label: Superhero plot narration
119563.note: General superhero plot with no single theme: the top sentence is Tony Stark inheriting Stark Industries (Iron Man), followed by Bruce as a billionaire vigilante and at the LexCorp gala (Batman v Superman), a 55-year-old Bruce in Dark Knight Returns, Bruce's obsession and a reckless chase in White Knight, Batman fighting Superman in Hush, and the Arkham patients taking over; it is in 20 Batman works and 3 cousins.

275969.label: Supporting-cast roundups
275969.note: Seven of eight sentences are cast-list sentences from the game articles ('Other characters appearing in the game include', 'Other characters marking their debut', 'Other characters include', 'Other villains include', characters that 'also appear', the game introducing a new villain), each naming characters with their voice actors; the Batman v Superman funeral sentence is the outlier.

505010.label: Talia al Ghul
505010.note: All eight top sentences name Talia, Ra's al Ghul's daughter: her voice casting and her immortality offer to the Joker in Arkham City, her kidnapping and her rescue of Catwoman in Hush, her Man-Bat Commandos in Batman R.I.P., and Tate revealing herself as Talia in Dark Knight Rises (present in 6 Batman works, no cousins).

429502.label: Lethal drug doses and antidotes
429502.note: All eight are about drugs given in doses or the antidotes to them (Crane's lethal dose and the two antidote vials in Batman Begins, Honor's heroin overdose, the single antidote dose in Arkham Asylum, Terry's antidote for Bruce, and three Knives Out medication and morphine-overdose sentences), so it is a general overdose-and-cure pattern, and 'poison' was too narrow because most of these are medicines or narcotics.

130837.label: Cast lists and character introductions
130837.note: Five of the eight are Wikipedia-style cast or debut notes (the Arkham Knight ally and cameo lists with voice actors, Talia's voice casting, the Arkham City supporting cast, Jean-Paul Valley's 'introduced in' publication note), while Margo Lane's meeting in The Shadow and two unrelated 'mutant' sentences (Mutant Leader, Ivy's mutant plants) do not fit, and a cast-list pattern is about how articles are written, not about Batman.

32476.label: Protégés (and 'Protocol 10')
32476.note: Five top sentences use protégé or protégée (Jason Todd twice, Terry McGinnis, Carrie Kelley, Shiwan Khan in The Shadow) and the other three are Arkham City's 'Protocol 10', so this layer-2 unit looks more like a detector for the 'prot-' word than for the mentor-and-sidekick idea.

866096.label: Characters named Lucy
866096.note: Four top sentences name Lucy outright (Lucy Ferrier with Jefferson Hope, Lucy Westenra's illness and the wolf attack in Dracula) and two more follow Lucy Ferrier's forbidden marriage and escape without naming her, while the outliers are Mina nursing her fiancé and the one Batman hit naming Lucius Fox, so it is mostly a cousin-work Lucy detector.

56706.label: The failed stand-up comedian
56706.note: Only half the top eight are the Joker's origin as a struggling comedian (Arthur Fleck's comedy-club routine and party-clown job in Joker 2019, the unnamed failed comedian twice in The Killing Joke); the other four are unrelated (the Arkham Knight cameo list, a Scarlet Pimpernel rescue, Robin accepted in Batman Forever, Nygma committed to Arkham).

63725.label: Two-Face
63725.note: Every top sentence names Two-Face or Harvey Dent: Grodd's alliance with him in Batman Ninja, the Arkham games' character lists, his coin swapped for a die in the Arkham Asylum comic, his bank heists in Arkham Knight, his post-therapy disappearance in Dark Knight Returns, and his reappearance on Halloween in The Long Halloween.

575002.label: Harley Quinn and Arkham
575002.note: Five of the eight name Harley Quinn (the Arkham Knight villain list, her attack on Napier in White Knight, her opera robbery in Hush, her return in Arkham City, the Tim Drake kidnapping in Return of the Joker), and the other three mention Arkham instead (Arkham State Hospital in Joker 2019, Deadshot infiltrating Arkham City, Grodd at Arkham Asylum in Batman Ninja), so it blends two related things.

875483.label: Franchise cast and publication notes
875483.note: All eight are behind-the-scenes Wikipedia notes rather than plot (the Arkham Knight villain's creators, the games' 'ensemble of characters from the history of Batman comics' and cameo lists, voice actors reprising roles, Knightfall's Batman #497 and the adding of Bane and Azrael to the cast), so it is article register that only looks Batman-specific because the Batman set contains game and comic articles.

557781.label: Dick Grayson, the first Robin
557781.note: Seven of the eight name Dick Grayson: as Jason's predecessor in Dark Knight Returns and Under the Red Hood, as the first Robin in A Death in the Family, as Nightwing leaving for Blüdhaven, at Elliot's funeral in Hush, in Batman & Robin, and as the Flying Graysons' survivor in Batman Forever; the one stray is an Iron Man sentence about Tony Stark's inheritance.

52211.label: Lucius Fox
52211.note: Five of the eight sentences name Lucius Fox as Bruce's tech supplier (Batman Begins, Knightfall, Earth One, Arkham Knight, Dark Knight Rises), but the three strongest hits are 2001's Clavius Base and Heywood Floyd, so this early-layer group (L4, 29 neurons) looks partly like a match on Latin '-ius' names (Lucius/Clavius) rather than a clean Fox detector.

564346.label: Heroes' families and supporting cast
564346.note: No single theme: it mixes Clark's adoptive father Jonathan (Superman, x3), the Joker capturing Jason Todd, teenage Bruce with Jessica and Harvey Dent, the Hush opera outing, Black Mask targeting Bruce and Lucius, and Bane's origin in Knightfall; the label only loosely covers about half of these, and it also fires in 3 cousin works.

874025.label: Gotham's districts and neighbourhoods
874025.note: Six of the eight sentences name parts of the city: the red-light district (Year One), Bleake, Founders and Miagani islands and Chinatown (Arkham Knight, x2), the 'Little Tokyo' section (1943 serial), the Narrows (Batman Begins) and Backport (White Knight); the other two (Joker's killings of trial officials, the Scarecrow evacuation) are city-wide civic events, and four hits contain the literal word 'district'.

513921.label: Lucius Fox
513921.note: Six of the eight sentences name Lucius Fox as the Wayne Enterprises tech ally (Batman Begins, The Dark Knight, Earth One, Arkham Knight, Knightfall, Dark Knight Rises); the other two are Zorro ('The Fox') and young Bruce seeing a Zorro movie in Batman R.I.P., so it responds to 'Fox' and to Zorro as well as to the character.

837276.label: Batman's wider supporting cast
837276.note: Every sentence is dense with named Batman characters, allies and villains alike (Talia revealed as Ra's daughter, the Graysons killed by Two-Face, Gordon with Dent, Barbara Gordon's promotion, Napier's disfigurement), but three of the eight are voice-cast or cameo lists from the Arkham games, so it partly tracks Wikipedia cast listings; it fires in no cousin works.

556414.label: DC lore places and femme fatales
556414.note: Two separate groups: named DC places (Fortress of Solitude in Lego Batman and Superman, the Phantom Zone, the Lazarus Pit, Arkham Castle) and female villains or antiheroes (Lady Shiva, Talia and Catwoman in Hush, Harley Quinn in White Knight and Hush, Lady Shiva in A Death in the Family); the Superman hit and 3 cousin works make it DC-wide, not Batman-only.

3666.label: Ultimatums (the word 'unless')
3666.note: A layer-0 word detector: all eight sentences contain 'unless', and seven are ultimatums (Jurassic Park's investors, Falcone, the Arkham inmates, Two-Face's bomb, Jason's gun, the Joker's hospital and ferries), while Puss in Boots' harmless 'unless he wants to' shows it keys on the word, not the idea; ultimatums are a general thriller pattern, not Batman-specific.

449052.label: The Batmobile
449052.note: Six of the eight sentences feature the Batmobile (Batman Ninja x2, White Knight, Dark Knight Returns, Batman Returns, Arkham Asylum); the two Fargo hits are the 'Oldsmobile', so this layer-0 unit is really matching the '-mobile' token, which in this corpus almost always means the Batmobile.

479291.label: No clear theme (Senator Finch)
479291.note: The top three are Batman v Superman scenes with Senator Finch and Lex Luthor, but the other five (a Batman R.I.P. rooftop, the Pimpernel's pepper snuff, Toy Story's Pizza Planet truck, Daredevil's Elektra, Bane watching Batman) share no visible idea.

564216.label: Bat-named gear and lairs
564216.note: All eight sentences contain a Bat- compound: the Bat aircraft (Dark Knight Rises), the Batmobile (Batman Returns), the Batcave (Lego Batman, Batman '89), the Bat-Signal (Batman v Superman, Batman & Robin), plus Batman Ninja's 'Batgod' and Bat Clan, which are not gear or lairs, so it is really a 'Bat-' prefix detector that mostly lands on equipment.
